notes.8: Question 8 Response B. This was the most popular response, although incorrect. Roughly equal numbers of candidates chose responses A and C. Candidates clearly thought that only one of the methods should work, although both would.
notes.11: Question 11 Response C. This response was more popular than the correct one. Candidates may have remembered the experiments they had seen, rather than thinking about the actual results which would be obtained.
notes.12: Question 12 In this question all of the responses were similarly popular, with response C being marginally the most popular.
notes.18: Question 18 Response B. Candidates seemed reluctant to decide that neither was correct, although they knew that the litmus answer was wrong.
notes.19: Question 19 Response C. Candidates knew that the oxides were covalent, but not of what type they were.
notes.27: Question 27 Response A. This was by far the most popular response, although wrong. Candidates clearly thought that two ‘no’ answers meant least reactive, but not fully understanding the implications of the oxide reacting with carbon.
notes.34: Question 34 Response D. Most candidates chose the correct alternative, but some were distracted by the mention of washing clothes in both the question and one of the responses.
notes.37: Question 37 Response B. Candidates understood what the question was about but, perhaps, misread ethane for ethene.
notes.general_comments: Candidates performed quite well on this paper. Questions 1, 2, 14, 15, 16 and 39 proved particularly straightforward with the majority of candidates choosing the correct response. Questions 8, 11, 12 and 27 proved to be difficult for candidates.
